full_judgment:
4. The defendant Nos. 1, 2, 3 and 11 contested the suit by filing separate sets of written statements. The case of these contesting defendants was that the suit land originally belonged to the defendant Nos. 5 to 8 who left this country for India and became Indian Nationals and, as such, the suit land vested in the government as enemy property. That the assistant custodian of enemy property granted settlement of the eastern side of the suit land to the Medical Association, Sylhet Branch and western side to the TB Association, Sylhet Branch and delivered possession thereof to the said lessees on 9-4-1970. That the settlement holders entered into possession of the suit land and constructed boundary walls. That the defendant No.4 had no right, title and interest in the suit land and consequently the plaintiffs could not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land by the alleged settlement. That the documents of the plaintiffs including rent receipts etc are false, fabricated and antedated and created for the purpose of the suit. That the alleged settlement of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs by the defendant No.4 was not permissible under section 10(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 5. The defendant No. 4 Sree Sree Radha Madhab Jew Deity represented by its Secretary also contested the suit by filing a separate written statement. This defendant has denied the material case of the plaintiffs and stated, inter-alia, that the defendant No. 4 is the owner in possession of the suit land, but this defendant never gave settlement of the suit land to the plaintiffs and the plaintiffs also never possessed the suit land. That the defendant No.4 deity had some temporary "Bharatias" in some portion of the suit land but subsequently those "Bharatias" left the suit land and the suit land came in khas possession of the defendant No.4. That the plaintiffs might have created some papers showing alleged settlement of the suit land in their favour in collusion with the "karmachari" of the defendant No.4, but those collusive papers were never acted upon. The further case of this defendant No.4 was that the government illegally acquired the suit land in LA Case No. 80/63-64 against which the defendant No.4 filed Title Suit No. 51 of 1964 against the government and others and that suit was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 33 of 1966 which was decreed on 28-10-1967 declaring title and possession of the defendant No.4 in the suit land. This defendant No.4 further stated that the suit land cannot be declared as enemy property and settled with the defendant No.3 or any other body as enemy property. That the suit land is in khas possession of the deity and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.
